'''''Gymnocalycium baldianum''''', the '''spider-cactus''' or '''dwarf chin cactus''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the cactus family Cactaceae, native to the [[Catamarca Province]] in [[Argentina]].

==Description==
It is a globose cactus, spherical or a little flat, with a diameter up to 8 cm, dark gray-green to blue-green in color, or sometimes brown, depressed, spherical shoots and reaches heights of 4 to 10 centimeters with diameters of 6 to 7 centimeters. It has 8 to 10 ribs with [[tubercle]]-shaped [[areole]]s, covered in groups of 6 to 8 pale grey, curved [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|spines]], giving to the species its common name of spider-cactus. Like many cacti, it does not divide but may form offsets after some years. There are no central spines. The five to seven gray or brown marginal thorns are thin, lie on the surface of the shoot and are up to 1.5 centimeters long.

The funnel-shaped flowers reach a diameter of 6 cm, growing near the apex of the plant and are red, pink or orange. Flowers are 3 to 5 centimeters long and reach the same diameter. The dark gray-green fruits are spindle-shaped.

==Distribution==
''Gymnocalycium baldianum'' is widespread in the Argentine province of Catamarca at altitudes of 1000 to 2000 meters.{{Citation needed|date=April 2025}}
==Taxonomy==
The first description as Echinocactus baldianus was made in 1905 by Carlos Luis Spegazzini.<ref name="Aires. 1905 t723">{{cite web | last=Aires. | first=Museo Nacional de Buenos | title=Anales del Museo Nacional de Buenos Aires | publisher=Impr. de Juan A. Alsina | volume=ser.3:t.4 (1905) | date=1905 | url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/4495375 | access-date=2023-09-23}}</ref> The specific epithet baldianum honors J. Baldi, an acquaintance and supporter of Carlos Luis Spegazzini. In 1925 he placed the species in the genus ''Gymnocalycium''.<ref name="Argentina Cient&amp Americano Cient&amp 1925 w043">{{cite web | last=Argentina | first=Sociedad Científica | last2=Cient&amp | first2=Congreso | last3=Americano | first3=fico Latino | last4=Cient&amp | first4=Congreso | title=Anales de la Sociedad Científica Argentina | publisher=[Sociedad Científica Argentina] | volume=t.99-100 (1925) | date=1925 | issn=0037-8437 | url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/48981237 | access-date=2023-09-23}}</ref>
==Cultivation==
''Gymnocalycium baldianum'' is easy to grow. It needs a well-drained soil. In summer, water the plants well, but let them to dry before watering again. Use monthly a fertilizer for cacti.<ref name = "art-biz"/> In winter, keep it dry, and the temperature may be as low as {{convert|-10 |C|F|abbr=on}}, but it is better to keep it without frost. The exposure must be sunny in summer and at least brightly lit in winter.

This species has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web
